children: Purchasing managers indexes for Mexico sent mixed messages in August. S&P Global's index fell to 49.8 from 51.3 in July, while the Inegi/Bank of Mexico PMI rose 2.1 points to 52.2 points and the Mexican Institute of Finance Executives' manufacturing index was unchanged at 49.7. "Mexican manufacturers signaled a renewed deterioration in operating conditions during August, with production falling at a quicker pace amid signs of softer demand conditions," S&P Global says. The firm noted pessimism around the year-ahead outlook, "as a number of manufacturers were downbeat about future sales pipelines, investment spending and general market uncertainty." (anthony.harrup@wsj.com)
